title: Drishyam The Conclusion show-sharing row: Panorama Studios’ Week 3 show demands put exhibitors in a fix as Nayyi Navelli, Prahaar, Jailer 2 gear up for release
raw_summary:
The much-loved Drishyam The Conclusion continues to remain steady at the box office. The Ajay Devgn-starrer crossed the Rs. 300 crore mark on Sunday, October 11, and is now expected to cross the Rs. 375 crore mark at the very least, with an outside chance of entering the coveted Rs. 400 crore club. The film has remained strong even on weekdays. As a result, its distributors, Panorama Studios, have asked cinemas to ensure that the thriller gets sufficient shows in its third week.

A trade source told Bollywood Hungama, “The distributors have asked single-screen cinemas to allot at least 3 shows to Drishyam The Conclusion from October 16. In two-screen theatres, they have sought 5 shows, while in three-screen cinemas, they have asked for 6 shows, including 1 morning show. In four-screen multiplexes, their request is for 7 shows, including 1 morning show, and in five-screen multiplexes, they have asked for 8 shows, including 1 morning show. In six-screen cinemas, they have sought 10 shows, while for theatres with seven screens or more, their demand is for 15 shows.”

The source continued, “Their request has put exhibitors in a dilemma, as several films are lined up for release this week, including Nayyi Navelli, Prahaar, Street Fighter, Jailer 2, Ranabaali, etc. All these films have the potential to attract audiences, including the last two, which will also release in Hindi. As a result, cinemas are trying to negotiate with the distributors of various films and arrive at a consensus.”

It is for this reason that advance bookings for the upcoming week are yet to open at several cinemas. When asked when the issue is likely to be resolved, the source replied, “It's difficult to say, going by recent experiences. The matter might be resolved by Wednesday morning or evening, or it could even extend to Thursday, just a day before the new releases arrive in cinemas.”

An industry insider commented, “Drishyam The Conclusion still has a lot of gas left in the tank and can continue to attract audiences despite the competition. The makers have also asked exhibitors to sell tickets at regular prices, which should further entice moviegoers.”

title: Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 release postponed to March 5, 2027
raw_summary:
Anupam Kher and Boman Irani’s Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 has received a new theatrical release date. The sequel, originally scheduled for release on August 28, 2026, will now hit cinemas on March 5, 2027.

The makers announced the revised date on social media with a new poster. Sharing the update, they wrote, “Deal Pakki! The Khoslas are ready to take possession of cinemas with #KhoslaKaGhosla2, arriving on the big screen on 5th March 2027!”

The announcement confirms a delay of several months for the sequel, which brings back characters from the much-loved 2006 comedy Khosla Ka Ghosla. The original film, directed by Dibakar Banerjee, revolved around a middle-class Delhi family caught up in a property dispute.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Anupam Kher (@anupampkher)

Anupam Kher and Boman Irani return to the franchise

Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 is directed by Prashant Bhagia and sees Anupam Kher and Boman Irani reprise their respective roles as Kamal Kishore Khosla and property dealer Kishan Khurana.

The returning cast also includes Ranvir Shorey, Parvin Dabas, Tara Sharma and Kiran Juneja. The sequel further features Ravi Kishan, Divya Khossla, Harsh Chhaya, Tanya Maniktala and Danish Iqbal, among others.

The makers have not revealed the full storyline yet. However, the sequel is expected to revisit the themes that defined the original film, including middle-class aspirations, property disputes and the schemes that emerge when the Khosla family finds itself dealing with another challenge.

Backed by T-Series Films and Tandav Films, the film is produced by Bhushan Kumar, Krishan Kumar, Savita Raj Hiremath and Raaj Hiremath. Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 is now scheduled to release in theatres on March 5, 2027.

title: Mrunal Thakur neither confirms nor denies Raaka casting rumours, says film announcements will come on social media
raw_summary:
Mrunal Thakur has addressed speculation about her possible involvement in Allu Arjun and Atlee’s upcoming film Raaka, but has stopped short of confirming whether she is part of the project. In a recent interview with HT City, the actor responded to questions about the rumours while keeping the focus on her latest release, Pooja Meri Jaan.

When asked directly if she was doing Raaka, Mrunal laughed and said, “I like how you assume that I am doing Raaka.” She added that she would announce her upcoming projects through her social media accounts, saying, “The announcement of upcoming films, I will make it on social networking sites soon, so that we put a full stop to all these rumours.” Mrunal Thakur wants to enjoy the process of acting Beyond the speculation surrounding her next projects, Mrunal spoke about her approach to choosing films and learning from each experience. She said, “I just want to enjoy the process. Because an experiment is like aim, apparatus, observation, conclusion, that’s it. I don’t want to come to a conclusion that it did not work. For me, everything is you live and you learn.”

The actor had addressed similar speculation in an earlier interview with Mid-Day. While she did not confirm or deny reports about her casting in Raaka, she said, “I haven't signed any film in almost nine months. I'm waiting for a meaningful role to come my way. Whatever announcement has to happen, it will happen on my social media handle, and then I'd love to talk about it.” What we know about Allu Arjun and Atlee's Raaka Raaka is the upcoming sci-fi film starring Allu Arjun and directed by Atlee. The project marks the first collaboration between the actor and the Tamil filmmaker and is scheduled for release in 2027. Deepika Padukone is also part of the film's lead cast. The ambitious pan-India project has already drawn attention for a Guinness World Record achievement in real-time motion capture, with 37 performers participating simultaneously.

According to sources, Sandhu will play a British-born Indian environmentalist who becomes involved in a mission that takes her into unexpected circumstances. However, further details about her character and the film’s storyline are being kept under wraps.

Produced by Vipul Amrutlal Shah under Sunshine Pictures and co-produced by Aashin A. Shah, Samuk marks Akshay Kumar and Shah’s collaboration after 13 years. The film is being mounted as a theatrical project and combines elements of science fiction, action and survival. Banita Sandhu joins an eclectic cast Sandhu has worked across Hindi and international projects since making her acting debut with Shoojit Sircar’s October. She later appeared in films including Sardar Udham and Main Vaapas Aaunga, besides featuring in the international series Bridgerton.

Her reported casting adds another name to Samuk’s ensemble, which also includes Rukmini Maitra, Vineet Kumar Singh, Rajat Kapoor and Swanand Kirkire, among others.

The makers have so far kept details about the characters largely under wraps. This has also led to curiosity around how the different actors fit into the film’s science-fiction world. Akshay Kumar and Vipul Amrutlal Shah reunite Samuk brings Akshay Kumar and producer Vipul Amrutlal Shah together after more than a decade. The two previously collaborated on projects including Namastey London, Singh Is Kinng and London Dreams.

With filming currently underway in London, more details about the film’s plot and characters are expected to emerge closer to its release. For now, the makers are keeping the storyline and individual character arcs closely guarded.

title: Rahul Vaidya passes beeped remark about Disha Parmar on Pati Patni Aur Panga 2; leaves contestants shocked as fans call him out on Reddit
raw_summary:
Singer Rahul Vaidya has landed in the middle of an online debate over a remark he made on the celebrity couple reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2. The comment, about his marriage to Disha Parmar, was beeped out on the show, but the reactions around him and a viral clip have kept the internet talking.

The show, hosted by Sonali Bendre and Munawar Faruqui, tests the marriage compatibility of celebrity couples through a series of games. In the round in question, Rahul, Vivek Dahiya and Parmeet Sethi were asked questions about their wives against a timer. Their wives, Disha Parmar, Divyanka Tripathi Dahiya and Archana Puran Singh, sat opposite and used their husbands' nicknames as buzzers.

The hosts asked the men to name five things their wives used to do before marriage but no longer do. Disha buzzed first, and Rahul was asked to answer. His response was completely beeped, and the audio does not make clear what he said. It drew an immediate reaction from everyone present.

Archana Puran Singh could not hide her shock. Mangal Lakshmi actress Deepika Singh said, "Allowed nahi hai TV pe bolna" (You cannot say this on TV). Disha asked him to stop. "Arrey mat hi bolo kuch, galat hi bologe, aur kya. Abhi chup raho" (Don't say anything at all, you will say something wrong only. Please keep quiet), she said. The hosts and others in the room were also visibly embarrassed. Rahul Vaidya claims on national television that his wife Disha Parmar doesn't give him s*x after Marriage. by u/RockstarRanger247 in IndianTellyTalk

Co-contestant Arjun Bijlani reacted sharply, asking, "Phir bachhe kaise ho rahein hai" (how are you having kids then). When Rahul tried to defend himself, saying, "Logon ko meri personal life mein bahut interests hai" (People are very interested in my personal life), Arjun's wife Neha Swamy responded, "Tu hi toh bata raha hai" (You are only saying it out loud).

A video of the moment has gone viral on Reddit. Many viewers in the comments have called out Rahul, saying he disrespected his wife by making such a remark on national television. Neither Rahul nor Disha has commented publicly on the reaction.

title: SCOOP: Playback sensation Heer of Batwara 1947 and Peddi fame to make acting debut in Imtiaz Ali and Mahaveer Jain’s Side Heroes

Both songs were composed by A R Rahman, who also composed the music for Ram Charan-starrer Peddi. In this Pan-India film, Heer lent her voice to the song 'Hellallallo'.

Her other recent songs include 'Roop Di Rani' from Pati Patni Aur Woh Do, alongside Guru Randhawa, and 'Chhaap Tilak' from Ginny Wedss Sunny 2. Both songs were composed by Tanishk Bagchi.

About Side Heroes

Side Heroes is a hilarious friendship-reunion film with a touch of nostalgia, set in the heartland of India. Besides Heer, ot stars Varun Sharma, Abhishek Banerjee and Aparshakti Khurana. It is produced by Imtiaz Ali, Mahaveer Jain, Mrighdeep Singh Lamba and Shikha K Ahluwalia, written by Siddarth Sen (director of Good Luck Jerry) and Pankaj Matta, and directed by Ssanjay Tripaathy.

In September, Bollywood Hungama exclusively reported that Side Heroes would be among the rare Hindi films to be shot entirely in Bihar. The film is scheduled to release on Friendship Day 2027.

Producer Ramesh Taurani recently reflected on the changing dynamics of Hindi film music in the 1990s and recalled how Alka Yagnik emerged as one of the most sought-after female playback singers of the decade. Taurani was speaking alongside his brother Kumar Taurani on Komal Nahta’s Game Changers: The Music Series.

Discussing the music landscape of the period, Ramesh Taurani recalled that established voices such as Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle continued to be important choices for filmmakers, while a new generation of singers was gaining prominence.

“Back then, Lata Ji and Asha Ji were already established. When we used to make music, Lata Ji was our first preference, followed by Alka and Anuradha,” Taurani said.

He went on to recall the emergence of singers including Kumar Sanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan. According to him, films such as Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Aashiqui, Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante helped establish the new voices in the industry as their songs became popular with audiences.

“The idea was that in the ’90s, when new singers like Shanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan came in, these four made it big. Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Aashiqui, Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante were hits, and their songs became superhits,” he recalled. How Alka Yagnik emerged as a leading female voice Taurani also drew a comparison between the newer singers and the established female playback voices of the previous generation. He recalled that Anuradha Paudwal was being viewed as a successor to Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik was increasingly being positioned as a voice comparable to Asha Bhosle.

“The idea then was that Anuradha Paudwal was the new Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik became the new Asha Bhosle,” Taurani said.

According to Taurani, the shift in Anuradha Paudwal’s film career eventually created more opportunities for Alka Yagnik. He recalled that after Paudwal stopped singing for films and became associated exclusively with T-Series, Alka began receiving a wider variety of female playback assignments.

“Luckily, Anuradha Ji stopped singing for films and made herself exclusive to T-Series. This worked in Alka Ji’s favour, as she got both Lata Ji and Asha Ji type songs, whether they were solos, duets or shayari,” he said.

Taurani further recalled the scale of Alka Yagnik’s presence during the period, saying she was receiving a significant number of songs compared with some of the leading male playback singers of the time.

“The situation was such that, among Udit, Sanu and Sonu, Alka Ji was getting the most songs,” he added.

The conversation featured Ramesh and Kumar Taurani discussing their experiences in the Hindi music industry and the changes they witnessed during the rise of the 1990s playback generation. The episode is part of Komal Nahta’s Game Changers: The Music Series, which focuses on conversations with singers, composers and other figures associated with Indian film music.

The clarification comes after reports suggested that the Hindi version of Jailer 2 could face restrictions over the gap between its theatrical release and OTT premiere. Some reports linked the situation to a four-week OTT window, reportedly connected to a larger digital rights deal. National multiplex chains such as PVR INOX and Cinepolis are generally associated with an eight-week theatrical-to-OTT window for Hindi films.

This led to speculation that the Hindi version of Jailer 2 could have a limited theatrical presence, particularly in the Hindi-speaking market. Jailer 2 team confirms October 15 Hindi release Putting the speculation to rest, the makers have stated that there has been no change to the film's planned Hindi theatrical release.

In their official statement, the team said, “In light of recent media reports suggesting that Jailer 2 will not be releasing in Hindi, we would like to officially clarify that the film’s Hindi version is scheduled for a theatrical release on Thursday, 15th October 2026, alongside its other language versions, as originally planned.”

The team also confirmed that the Hindi version will have a distributor for the North Indian market. “The film will be distributed in North India by Pen Marudhar Entertainment,” the statement read.

The makers further reiterated that the release schedule remains unchanged, adding, “There has been no change to the scheduled Hindi theatrical release.” Makers ask media to avoid unverified information The statement also addressed the circulation of reports suggesting that the film's Hindi release had been affected.

“We request all media publications and platforms to take note of this clarification and refrain from circulating any unverified information regarding the film’s release,” the team said.

The makers concluded by thanking the media for its support and cooperation.

With the latest clarification, the Jailer 2 team has officially maintained that the Hindi version will release theatrically on October 15 along with the film's other language versions. Pen Marudhar Entertainment will handle its distribution across North India.

The film is the sequel to Rajinikanth's 2023 blockbuster Jailer. Further details regarding the film's theatrical rollout and show distribution are awaited.

title: Rian Mukherjee wins Best Child Actor at Los Angeles Film Awards 2026 for Hindi film Manzil
raw_summary:
Debutant actor Rian Mukherjee wins the Best Child Actor Award at the prestigious Los Angeles Film Awards 2026 for his Hindi film Manzil. Directed by his father and National Award-winning filmmaker Ram Kamal Mukherjee, the lead actors of the film are Rituparna Sengupta, Sanjay Suri, and Abhishek Kumar. Produced under the banners of Dhanbad Talkies and Endeavour Films, the film follows the journey of a writer and a photographer who accidentally meet at a resort.

Rian plays the role of Aron, son of writer Ananya, played by Rituparna Sengupta, who becomes an integral part of the narrative through his presence. "I am delighted that the jury members felt Rian's performance was worth recognition," says his father and filmmaker Ram Kamal Mukherjee. "I think he is a gifted actor, as he never had any formal training, yet he faced the camera and knew his lines by heart," he added.

Rituparna Sengupta, who plays Rian's mother in the film, was thrilled as well. "I have literally seen him grow before my eyes. I still remember seeing Rian when he was born. Ram and Sarbani are like family, and when Ram decided to cast Rian as my son in the film, I knew he would leave an impact," added Rituparna, who also dons the hat of creative producer for the film. Produced by Rajesh Singh and Sharmistha Mukherjee, the film is currently making the rounds at festivals globally. "Rian is a promising actor from India. He competed with international child actors and emerged as a winner because of his natural screen presence and restrained voice modulation in the given space," added jury member and veteran actor Jean Vincentelli.

The first look at this film was exclusively showcased at an award ceremony in Mumbai, where Rian's screen presence was appreciated by prominent actors present at the ceremony.

Rian is the only Indian to win at LAFA 2026, while the other winners are Jingnu Ning, who won the Best Picture Award for his film A Palmful of Stars, and Phil Aman, who won the Best Actor trophy for Soundcheck. Nazakati Maihemuti bagged Best Actress for A Palmful Of Stars. "I am an accidental actor," says Rian Mukherjee. "I enjoy acting because that's the only time I get to see my Baba at work. He is extremely sincere towards his craft."

title: Sharvari named first-ever brand ambassador of Reva by PNGS
raw_summary:
Reva, the certified natural diamond jewellery brand of PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Limited, announced actor Sharvari as its brand ambassador. This is the first time Reva has partnered with a celebrity face, marking a milestone moment for the brand just months after its listing on the stock exchanges in March 2026, and as it embarks on its most ambitious expansion yet.

Sharvari is one of Hindi cinema’s most exciting young leads, with a growing body of work that spans diverse genres, from horror-comedy and action to romance. She made her big-screen debut with Bunty Aur Babli 2 and has since been seen in Munjya, Maharaj, Vedaa, Main Vaapas Aaunga and YRF’s Alpha. She will next be seen in Sooraj Barjatya’s Yeh Prem Mol Liya, slated for release in November. Sharvari will be the face of Reva’s brand campaigns across print, digital, outdoor and in-store, beginning with the festive and wedding season.

Amit Modak, CEO, PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Limited, said, "Reva is entering a defining phase. Since our listing, we have been expanding with clarity, opening exclusive stores, launching our online platform and preparing to take the brand into new cities, including key markets in North India. As we grow beyond our home ground, we need a face that resonates nationally while staying true to who we are. Sharvari does exactly that. Her appeal cuts across regions and age groups, and she will help us introduce Reva and the value of a certified natural diamond to many more customers across India."

Aditya Modak, Director, Reva by PNGS, said, "Our very first brand ambassador had to be someone who truly reflects the Reva woman, and Sharvari was a natural choice in every sense. She is rooted, she is real, and she has earned her place through her own effort, much like a natural diamond is shaped over time. Today's woman buys diamonds not only for weddings but for herself, for her milestones and for her every day. Sharvari embodies that confidence, and together we want to make natural diamonds a part of more women's stories."

Sharvari, Brand Ambassador, Reva, said, “Being the first face of Reva makes this association especially exciting for me. As a Maharashtrian, P. N. Gadgil & Sons is a name I’ve known and associated with trust and tradition for as long as I can remember. What drew me to Reva is how it brings natural diamonds into the everyday, with designs that feel modern while still holding on to the timelessness of the stone. I’m happy to be part of a brand that makes diamonds feel relevant to different moments in a woman’s life, from ordinary days to the most special occasions.”

The Sharvari partnership comes as Reva accelerates its retail and digital expansion. The brand currently operates 38 stores, comprising 5 exclusive brand outlets and 34 shop-in-shop counters within the P. N. Gadgil & Sons network, with a strong presence across Maharashtra and a growing footprint in Gujarat and Karnataka. Recent openings include exclusive stores at Amanora Mall, Pune (July 2026) and Nashik (September 2026).

Following its IPO in March 2026, Reva is on track to open around 15 new company-owned exclusive stores within 24 months of listing. The rollout will focus primarily on Tier 1 cities, with selective expansion into Tier 2 cities and metro markets across Maharashtra and key North India markets. In September 2026, Reva also launched its e-commerce platform, revadiamonds.com, bringing its collections to customers across the country. With a pan-India appeal, Sharvari will be central to introducing Reva to these new markets and a new generation of diamond buyers.

title: Guru Randhawa announces The Sirra Era Live In Concert in Delhi on December 12; details inside
raw_summary:
Guru Randhawa is set to return to the live concert stage with ‘The Sirra Era Live In Concert’, a stadium show scheduled to take place at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi on December 12, 2026. The event will mark his first solo stadium concert and his return to major live performances after a three-year touring hiatus.

Produced by Saregama Live in association with Rhythms and Warner Music India, the concert will bring together songs from Randhawa’s career, including some of his popular hits and more recent releases. The announcement also marks his first major live engagement in the national capital since 2023 and follows his last full-scale domestic tour in 2022. Guru Randhawa calls concert a thank-you to fans Speaking about his return to the stage, Randhawa said the break from touring was planned and described the upcoming concert as an opportunity to reconnect with the fans who have supported him throughout his career.

“Taking a step back from touring was a planned pause, but standing here now, ready to step into a stadium, is incredibly surreal. My fans have been the absolute bedrock of this amazing journey, holding me up through every high and every low. This show isn't about me alone, it's my humble thank-you note to the people who built me. I wanted this homecoming to happen exactly where it all started, looking out at a stadium full of the faces who changed my life, and giving that love and respect straight back to my day ones!” he said.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Guru Randhawa (@gururandhawa)

The singer’s upcoming performance is being positioned as a celebration of his 13-year journey in the music industry and his connection with listeners. The concert will feature tracks such as ‘Lahore’, ‘High Rated Gabru’, ‘Suit Suit’, ‘Patola’, ‘Naach Meri Rani’, ‘Made In India’, ‘Slowly Slowly’ and ‘Ban Ja Rani’. His more recent releases, including ‘Dopamine’, ‘AZUL’, ‘SHKINI’, ‘PERFECT’, ‘Qatal’ and ‘Sirra’, are also part of the announced song catalogue. Saregama Live on the scale of the concert Siddharth Anand Kumar, Executive Vice President of Films, Series and Events at Saregama India, said the concert aims to bring Randhawa’s music to a larger audience through a stadium-scale event. He also spoke about the wider role of live entertainment in bringing artists and audiences together.

“Guru Randhawa’s music has a massive connect with audiences, and bringing him to a stadium in Delhi is about taking that connect to a larger scale. For us at Saregama, live entertainment is as much about bringing artists closer to their audiences as it is about building a strong ecosystem around these experiences. Shows like these bring together multiple teams, partners and businesses, all working towards one shared goal: delivering a great experience for fans. It’s this collective effort that makes the live entertainment business exciting, and we’re happy to continue being a part of it,” Kumar said.

According to the organisers, ‘The Sirra Era Live In Concert’ will feature large-scale production and audio-visual elements designed for a stadium setting. They have also said that environmentally conscious practices will be incorporated wherever feasible during the event’s planning and execution.

Scheduled as a one-night-only show, the concert will see Randhawa perform for audiences in New Delhi as he resumes major live engagements. Further details about ticket sales and availability were not included in the announcement.

A source told Bollywood Hungama, “The film is titled Hum Tere Pyaar Mein. The title is apt for the story and, moreover, it has an old-school touch and charm, which is sure to appeal to audiences across age groups.”

Hum Tere Pyaar Mein also marks the directorial debut of Vidhi Ghodgaonkar, who has spent 17 years working closely with Rohit Shetty as his protégé. She has worked as an assistant director on films like Golmaal 3 (2010), Singham (2011), Bol Bachchan (2012), Chennai Express (2013), Singham Returns (2014), Dilwale (2015), Golmaal Again (2017) and Simmba (2018), as well as the web series Indian Police Force (2024). She was also a part of the writing team of Sooryavanshi (2021), Cirkus, Indian Police Force and Singham Again (2024).

Hum Tere Pyaar Mein is produced by Abhishek S Vyas under the banner of AVS Studios in association with Tudip Entertainment.

Interestingly, Krithi Shetty is no stranger to Hindi cinema. She began her acting career with a small role in the Hrithik Roshan-starrer Super 30 (2019). However, her full-fledged debut as a leading actress came with the Telugu film Uppena (2021). She subsequently appeared in films like Shyam Singha Roy (2021), Bangarraju (2022), Custody (2023), Manamey (2024), ARM (2024), etc. Over the years, she has made a mark not just in Telugu cinema but also in Tamil and Malayalam films. With Hum Tere Pyaar Mein, she is now set to embark on a new chapter in Bollywood.

title: Adivi Sesh writes to Assam government over reported resort development near Kaziranga National Park
raw_summary:
Actor Adivi Sesh has written to the Assam government expressing concern over reports of resort development on land associated with Kaziranga National Park. In his letter, the actor urged the authorities to examine the potential environmental impact of the proposed development and prioritise wildlife conservation and the interests of local communities.

Kaziranga, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is known for its biodiversity and population of the endangered greater one-horned rhinoceros. Concerns over construction and tourism infrastructure in ecologically sensitive areas have raised questions about how development can be balanced with the protection of wildlife habitats and natural corridors.

In his letter, Adivi called for greater transparency regarding the land involved and urged the government to assess the possible long-term consequences of the proposed development before making decisions that could affect the region’s ecosystem.

“Nature does not belong to us; we are only its temporary custodians,” he said, highlighting the importance of protecting Kaziranga’s wildlife and natural heritage. Adivi Sesh calls for responsible tourism Acknowledging the economic benefits of tourism, Adivi said development in ecologically sensitive regions should be guided by long-term environmental considerations.

“I understand that tourism can generate employment, create opportunities and contribute to the local economy. But development must be planned with a long-term vision, particularly when it concerns ecologically sensitive regions,” he said.

The actor also questioned whether commercial development was necessary in every area, pointing to the potential consequences for wildlife and the environment.

“Sustainable tourism should be about experiencing nature while preserving it, not about changing the very landscape that makes a place special in the first place,” he added.

Adivi also highlighted the importance of protecting wildlife corridors, warning that habitat loss and disruptions to natural ecosystems can be difficult to reverse. He referred to the greater one-horned rhinoceros as a symbol of Assam’s biodiversity and stressed the need to safeguard its habitat. Actor highlights concerns of local communities Beyond wildlife conservation, Adivi said decisions concerning development around Kaziranga should take into account the people who have lived in the region for generations.

“My concern extends beyond the rhinos and the wildlife that call Kaziranga home. There are local communities who have lived in and around this landscape for generations, whose lives, livelihoods and traditions are deeply connected to the land,” he said.

He added that these communities should have a voice in decisions affecting their surroundings, arguing that conservation efforts must consider both the environment and the people who depend on it. Adivi urges Assam government to review proposed development In his appeal, Adivi urged the Assam government to carefully review the implications of the reported resort development, make information about the land publicly available and commission independent environmental assessments wherever necessary.

“I hope that all relevant ecological, legal and community considerations are examined before any irreversible decisions are made. This is not about opposing development; it is about asking for development that is thoughtful, responsible and sustainable,” he said.

The actor concluded by stressing the importance of preserving Kaziranga for future generations, including its wildlife, forests and surrounding communities.

The letter adds to the broader debate over tourism infrastructure and conservation in ecologically sensitive regions. The details of the reported approval, including the precise location and environmental implications of the proposed resort, would need to be established through official records and assessments.
